title: Jude and the Crown
premise: When the border wards sealing the valley of Hollowmere collapse on the night the stars go out, runaway apprentice Ivo Blackwood discovers her hedge-magic — useless inside the valley — is the last living thread of an ancient covenant between the human realm and the starlit court beyond. Hunted by the Crown's wardens who want the covenant reforged under their control, and guided by Jude, a disgraced royal cartographer who knows what the old kings buried, Ivo must reach the fallen Starwell before the solstice. There she learns the covenant was never broken by accident: the Crown itself devoured it for power, and restoring it means surrendering that power forever. In the end, Ivo chooses to bind the magic not to any throne but to a chosen family of outcasts, reigniting the stars and unmaking the Crown's claim over both realms.
about_author: Wren Sandoval is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval land charters before turning to fantasy, and their love of borders, maps, and broken oaths saturates every page they write. They live at the edge of a national forest with two opinionated goats and a growing collection of antique compasses.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the eve of her escape from her mistress's cottage, the valley's perpetual gloom deepens as every star vanishes, and the ancient wards at the valley mouth shatter like glass. Ivo feels magic flood into her for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined as the world she resented becomes the world she may lose.

chapters.title: What the Hedge Taught Her
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Fleeing through the darkened valley, Ivo passes dying villages where hedge-charms fail and livestock sickens. She reaches her estranged mistress, Maren, who reveals Ivo's bloodline ties to the covenant's original keepers — then dies holding the door against warden scouts. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve; the past she ran from is now her inheritance.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Crime
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the Crown city of Vaelport, disgraced royal cartographer Jude Ashgrave is dragged from prison because his forbidden maps mark the Starwell's location. The Lord Warden offers him pardon for one journey — as bait for the 'keeper' the wards' fall will surely draw out. Emotional beat: bitter pragmatism masking shame over what he once mapped for the Crown.

chapters.title: Out of the Valley
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo crosses the broken border into a starless world where her small magic suddenly roars — flowers bloom at her footsteps, wards spark off her skin. She is ambushed by wardens, saved by a feral girl named Sef who steals her supplies and then her trust. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into wariness; outside the valley, everything costs something.

chapters.title: An Unlikely Company
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude intercepts Ivo and Sef on the pilgrim road, posing as a fellow traveler while reporting their position by coded letter. But watching Ivo heal a plague-struck farm family for free unsettles his cynicism. When he burns the letter instead of sending it, he crosses a line. Emotional beat: the first crack in a man built for betrayal.

chapters.title: The Road of Hollow Kings
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The trio follows Jude's map along an ancient processional road lined with toppled statues of kings whose faces were chiseled away. Ivo learns the statues aren't defaced — they're devouring, drinking light even now. At night she dreams of a voice calling from beneath the Starwell. Emotional beat: dread deepening; the enemy is older and stranger than the Crown.

chapters.title: Sef's Price
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Flashback-woven chapter revealing Sef was a court child sold to the wardens' kennels, escaped with a brand that lets them track her. She hides the truth until the brand flares during a checkpoint crossing, forcing a violent escape that leaves Jude wounded. Emotional beat: found-family bonds tested by secrets; Sef choosing trust over survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Warden's Mercy
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. While Ivo tends Jude's fever, he confesses his crime: years ago he mapped the Starwell so the Crown could drain it, believing the realms' separation caused a famine. The Lord Warden arrives offering Jude full restoration if he delivers Ivo. Jude refuses aloud — knowing refusal means both their deaths now. Emotional beat: confession as rebirth; loyalty chosen at cost.

chapters.title: City of Salt and Bells
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Hiding in the free-city of Brackwater, the trio finds allies among covenant-descended outcasts: a deaf bell-founder, Tam, who casts charms in bronze, and a defected warden sergeant, Orla. Together they learn the Crown plans to reforge the covenant at solstice — bound to the throne, enslaving the star-court. Emotional beat: hope kindling; Ivo stops being alone.

chapters.title: What Power Wants
chapters.summary: Orla's POV. Orla reveals the Lord Warden's true design: he doesn't serve the Crown but intends to replace it, using the covenant's power to become a god-warden. A raid on Brackwater's safehouse scatters the group; Tam is captured carrying the forged bell-key they need. Emotional beat: fury and guilt; the cost of resistance made flesh.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following the voice from her dreams, Ivo dives into a flooded chapel where the covenant's first keeper left a memory-trap. Inside it she experiences the original binding — and learns the covenant was always meant to be held by many hands, never one. She surfaces changed, able to hear the star-court's dying song. Emotional beat: awe and burden; knowledge that cannot be unkown.

chapters.title: Bargains in the Dark
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. To rescue Tam, Jude walks back into Vaelport and offers the Lord Warden exactly what he wants — himself, maps, and Ivo's route — playing triple agent while Orla and Sef run the real rescue. The extraction succeeds, but the Warden lets them go, having learned all he needs. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by the suspicion of being played.

chapters.title: The Solstice Road
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Racing north as the days shorten unnaturally, the company endures a blizzard of falling ash — the sky itself failing without the star-court's anchor. Ivo's power grows unstable, burning what she loves; she nearly kills Sef in her sleep. Emotional beat: fear of self; power as corruption beginning in the heroine too.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sheltering in a ruined waystation, Ivo finally reads Maren's hidden letter: her mistress knew Ivo would be the one to face the Starwell and chose harshness to make her strong enough to refuse its temptations. Grief transmutes into purpose. The company swears an oath to each other, not the Crown. Emotional beat: catharsis; found family formalized.

chapters.title: The Gate of Thorns
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The final approach to the Starwell is a hedge of living thorns grown from the old covenant's corpse, which tests each traveler with their deepest want. Jude sees his name restored in marble; Orla sees her dead unit alive; Sef sees the kennels empty. Only Ivo sees nothing — and that emptiness lets her lead them through. Emotional beat: desire confronted and refused.

chapters.title: The Starwell
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. They reach the Starwell: a vast crater where a dead star lies caged in chains of crown-iron, its light hoarded by the Crown for generations. The star-court's last envoy, a moth-winged figure named Vess, tells Ivo the truth — restore the covenant and the realms reopen, but someone must stand at the center and hold it. Forever, or die trying. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; the price named at last.

chapters.title: The Lord Warden Ascendant
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Lord Warden arrives with the royal host and Tam in chains, demanding Ivo bind the covenant to him. He demonstrates his stolen power by snuffing the moon. Jude, publicly pardoned and reinstated, kneels — then uses his restored access to shatter the Warden's anchor-staff, buying seconds with his own arrest. Emotional beat: sacrifice completing redemption; the traitor's final loyalty.

chapters.title: Crown of Iron, Crown of Light
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Climax. As wardens and outcasts clash across the crater rim, Ivo enters the well and begins the reforging. The Warden breaks free and seizes the binding, and for one annihilating moment Ivo feels what absolute power feels like — and understands why the old kings fell. She lets go, passing the covenant outward through every hand joined around the well. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; power shared or lost entirely.

chapters.title: Many Hands
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. The covenant catches through the circle — Sef, Orla, Tam, wounded Jude, even defecting wardens — each becoming a keeper. The Lord Warden, refusing to share, is unmade by the very power he tried to monopolize, dissolving into ordinary mortal dust. The dead star reignites and climbs back into the sky. Emotional beat: exaltation through communion; the many overcoming the one.

chapters.title: Stars Over Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The valley's wards rise again — but open now, gates instead of walls. Ivo returns home to bury Maren properly and finds the villagers no longer strangers but neighbors under a starred sky. Magic flows gently again, held by hundreds of keepers rather than hoarded by any crown. Emotional beat: homecoming transformed; the place she fled becomes the place she chose.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's New Map
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Epilogue-set chapter. Jude drafts a new map of two realms joined by open roads, deliberately leaving blank spaces marked 'uncharted — go see.' He and Ivo argue cheerfully about scale while Sef and Orla plan the first embassy to the star-court. Emotional beat: warmth and forward motion; endings as beginnings.

chapters.title: A Covenant Kept
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Final chapter, one year later. At the solstice festival in Hollowmere, keepers from both realms renew the covenant by hand — no throne, no altar, just people. Ivo takes an apprentice of her own, a frightened valley kid like she once was, and teaches her the first lesson Maren never got to finish: magic follows trust, not command. Emotional beat: quiet fulfillment; justice lived daily outside the law.
